subject: Improve efficiency for categorical factor analysis model?

messages.author: 07019e4ee91b7432
messages.subject: Improve efficiency for categorical factor analysis model?
parts:
Hello Stan Users,

I am estimating a series of factor analysis models with 2 correlated factors and 10 binary indicators (this is also a multidimensional item response theory model, and the same model I posted about here). 

Previously I scaled the latent factors N(0,1) and estimated the covariance between them, but because of the previous thread about sign indeterminacy, I now scale the latent factors by setting one factor loading =1 for each factor and estimating the variance and covariance for both factors. This has solved the sign indeterminacy issue, but the reparameterized model is performing more poorly in terms of effective sample size and Rhat. 

I've run this on 500 simulated data sets. With 2 chains and 10,000 iterations each (half warmup), in 11 of the 500 replications, Rhat is above 1.1 and n_eff is less than 50 for 1 or more parameters (I count this as a "failed" replication). In the remaining 489 replications, average n_eff seems much too low to me (tabled below). 
---------------------------------------------------------
 parmType   Mean Est   Avg n_eff   Min n_eff   Max n_eff 
---------- ---------- ----------- ----------- -----------
   cov       0.301       4808        2020        6637    
  lambda      1.11       318.7       70.22       627.1   
    nu      0.003462     7005        987.1       10000   
sigma[1,1]   2.126       203.7       50.09       355.3   
sigma[1,2]   0.6166      444.2       63.29       1181    
sigma[2,1]   0.6166      444.2       63.29       1181    
sigma[2,2]   2.135       204.6       58.46       357.7   
---------------------------------------------------------
I have tried to optimize by expressing the covariance matrix as a cholesky factor and vectorizing when possible. My understanding is that the "matt trick" doesn't apply here, because I'm only estimating the covariance matrix (means are set to zero for the latent factors).

I'm attaching an example program and data set. Are there suggestions to improve this model? 

In this condition and example data set, each indicator has p=.5 probability of endorsement. Ultimately, I am interested in using this model when the probability of endorsement is low for some items and using priors to stabilize the parameter estimates. In theory, this should be a big improvement over ML, however at the moment I am having trouble getting good performance for this baseline condition. The low probability conditions are, of course, much worse.

I used the following code in R to read in the example data and fit the model:
dat<-read.table("data1.dat", header=FALSE)
N<-500
K<-10
F<-2
cfa.data<-list(N=N,K=K,F=F,y=dat)
Nchains<-2
Niter<-10000

#compile model
model=rstan::stan_model(file='cfa2factor-chol2.stan')
#evaluate model
out=rstan::sampling(object = model
                    , data=cfa.data
                    , chains=Nchains
                    , iter=Niter
                    , warmup=Niter/2
                    , refresh=Niter/10
                    , seed=1)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Improve efficiency for categorical factor analysis model?
parts:
For scaling other than unit scaling, Stan has to figure
out the scale during adaptation.

Non-centering (what we used to call the "Matt trick")
refers to *both* the mean and the log scale. And it makes
an even bigger difference in multiple dimensions.

- Bob
